topic: Credit card minimum due: how little of it clears your bill
hook_pattern: contrarian-number (the minimum due barely touches the bill)
caption:
Paid only the minimum due on your credit card? Most of it never touched the bill.

Illustrative example: a ₹50,000 bill, interest at 3.5% a month (cards in India commonly charge about 2.5–4% a month, roughly 30–48% a year) and a minimum due of 5%.

You pay the ₹2,500 minimum. About ₹1,750 of the next month's charge is interest, so only about ₹750 actually cuts what you owe. Keep paying only the minimum with no new spends and it could take around 15 years and roughly ₹99,000 in interest to clear (illustrative, assuming a ₹200 minimum floor; GST on interest and late fees would add more).

Pay a fixed ₹5,000 a month instead and the same bill clears in about 13 months, with about ₹12,600 of interest. Paying the full bill by the due date costs no interest at all.

Three fixes: pay the full bill if you can, set a fixed payment well above the minimum if you can't, and stop new spends on that card until it's clear.

Save this. Send it to someone who pays only the minimum.

Sources: published guides to Indian credit card interest rates and how the minimum due works (2026). Rupee amounts are our illustrative calculations.
For education only. Not investment advice.
